title: Intermediate Core
description: Words you meet in news, school and work. The bridge from conversation to reading.

words.definition: to succeed in doing something after hard work
examples: She *achieved* her goal of running a marathon.
You can *achieve* a lot if you work hard.

words.definition: to change to fit a new situation
examples: It took me a month to *adapt* to the new school.
Animals *adapt* to their environment.
words.note: adapt TO something. Don't confuse with adopt (= take as your own).

words.definition: to study something carefully to understand it
examples: Scientists *analyzed* the data.
Let's *analyze* why the plan failed.

words.definition: a way of dealing with something; to come near
examples: We need a new *approach* to this problem.
A stranger *approached* me on the street.
words.note: The verb takes no preposition: approach a person (not "approach to").

words.definition: to think that something is true without having proof
examples: I *assumed* you already knew.
Don't *assume* everyone agrees with you.

words.definition: knowing that something exists or is happening
examples: Are you *aware* of the risks?
I wasn't *aware* that the store was closed.
words.note: aware OF something / aware THAT... Noun: awareness.

words.definition: an advantage or good result that something gives you
examples: Exercise has many health *benefits*.
Everyone will *benefit* from the new library.

words.definition: something difficult that tests your ability
examples: Learning a new language is a big *challenge*.
She likes to *challenge* herself.

words.definition: a result of an action, often a bad one
examples: If you break the rules, there will be *consequences*.
Rising sea levels are a *consequence* of global warming.

words.definition: to think carefully about something before deciding
examples: I'm *considering* changing jobs.
Please *consider* my offer.

words.definition: to give something to help a group or cause a result
examples: Everyone *contributed* ideas to the project.
Stress can *contribute* to illness.

words.definition: extremely important
examples: Sleep is *crucial* for good health.
This is a *crucial* moment in the game.

words.definition: to find out the facts; to decide or control what happens
examples: Police are trying to *determine* the cause of the fire.
Your choices *determine* your future.
words.note: Adjective: determined (= having a strong will).

words.definition: working well without wasting time, money or energy
examples: This new heater is very *efficient*.
She's an *efficient* worker.
words.note: Not the same as effective (= produces the result you want). Noun: efficiency.

words.definition: in the end, after a long time or many problems
examples: He *eventually* found a job.
Don't worry, you'll *eventually* get used to it.
words.note: It does NOT mean "possibly" — a common learner mistake.

words.definition: facts or signs that show something is true
examples: There is no *evidence* that he took the money.
Scientists found *evidence* of water on Mars.

words.definition: able to bend easily; able to change easily
examples: I have a *flexible* schedule.
Yoga makes your body more *flexible*.

words.definition: happening often
examples: She is a *frequent* visitor to our shop.
*Frequent* exercise is good for your heart.

words.definition: to recognize someone or something and say who or what they are
examples: Can you *identify* the man in the photo?
We need to *identify* the problem first.

words.definition: the power to change how someone thinks or acts
examples: My grandfather had a big *influence* on me.
Advertising *influences* what we buy.
words.note: Noun: influence ON someone. Verb: no preposition.

words.definition: to keep something in good condition or at the same level
examples: It's hard to *maintain* a healthy diet.
The building is well *maintained*.

words.definition: easy to see or understand
examples: The answer is *obvious*.
It was *obvious* that she was tired.

words.definition: to take part in an activity or event
examples: All students must *participate* in the discussion.
Over 500 runners *participated* in the race.

words.definition: a particular way of thinking about something
examples: Traveling gave me a new *perspective* on life.
Try to see it from my *perspective*.

words.definition: something that is more important than other things
examples: My family is my top *priority*.
Safety is our first *priority*.

words.definition: not wanting to do something
examples: He was *reluctant* to ask for help.
She gave a *reluctant* smile.

words.definition: to need something; to make something necessary
examples: This job *requires* a lot of patience.
Passengers are *required* to wear seat belts.

words.definition: large or important enough to be noticed or to have an effect
examples: There has been a *significant* increase in prices.
Her birthday is a *significant* date for me.

words.definition: a plan for achieving a goal
examples: What's your *strategy* for learning vocabulary?
The company changed its marketing *strategy*.

words.definition: to usually do something or be a certain way
examples: I *tend* to eat too much when I'm stressed.
Prices *tend* to rise in summer.
